lead: A polymer is a large molecule built by joining many small monomer units. The repeat unit is the part that repeats along the chain, and the degree of polymerisation tells how many such units are joined. Polymers are classified by source, heat behaviour, chain shape, and number of monomer types. This classification helps predict properties and choose materials, from a PET water bottle to a jute bag. Understanding these terms is the first step to naming and using polymers correctly.
prereq: You need Unit 1 for covalent bonding and the tetrahedral carbon backbone.

sections.h3: Monomer, repeat unit and degree of polymerisation

blocks.text: A monomer is a small molecule that can join with others. Ethylene (C₂H₄) is a monomer. A polymer forms when many monomers join. The part that repeats along the chain is the repeat unit (some syllabi call it the mer). For polyethylene, the repeat unit is –CH₂–CH₂–.

The degree of polymerisation (DP) is the number of repeat units in one polymer chain. DP is a whole number. A chain with DP = 500 has 500 repeat units. An oligomer is a short polymer with DP between about 2 and 10. It behaves more like a small molecule.

For a chain to grow, each monomer must have functionality of at least two. Functionality is the number of reactive sites that can form bonds. Ethylene has a double bond that opens to give two bonds, so functionality = 2. A molecule with only one reactive site cannot extend a chain.

The molar mass of a polymer sample is an average because chains have different DP values. The DP worked out from a sample's molar mass is therefore an average degree of polymerisation, not the DP of one chain. We name average molar mass here and give formulas in 5.7.
A homopolymer has only one type of monomer. Polyethylene from ethylene only is a homopolymer. A copolymer has two or more types of monomer joined in the same chain. The arrangement matters.

items: Random copolymer: monomers arranged randomly. Example: styrene-butadiene rubber.
Alternating copolymer: monomers alternate strictly A-B-A-B.
Block copolymer: long stretches of one monomer then long stretches of another. Example: SBS rubber (styrene-butadiene-styrene).
Graft copolymer: a chain of one monomer is attached as a branch to a backbone of another.

blocks.text: The number of monomer types is a classification axis: homopolymer vs copolymer. Tacticity, the order of side groups, is separate and covered in 5.2.

sections.h3: Classification by source, heat behaviour and chain shape

blocks.text: By source: Natural polymers come from plants or animals. Examples: starch, cellulose (jute), natural rubber. Semi-synthetic polymers are natural polymers modified chemically. Example: cellulose acetate. Synthetic polymers are made in factories. Examples: polyethylene (PE), polyvinyl chloride (PVC), PET.

By heat behaviour: Thermoplastic softens on heating and can be reshaped. Examples: PE, PVC. Thermoset does not soften on heating because chains are heavily cross-linked. Example: bakelite. Elastomer is a polymer that stretches and returns when the force is removed. Conventional rubbers are lightly cross-linked after vulcanisation, and natural rubber itself is an elastomer.
By chain shape: Linear chains have no branches. Example: HDPE. Branched chains have side branches. Example: LDPE. Cross-linked chains are joined by covalent bonds between chains. Example: bakelite.

By mechanism: chain-growth (often addition) and step-growth (often condensation). The two pairs are not identical: chain-growth is not always addition, and step-growth is not always condensation. Polyurethane forms by step-growth but not by condensation. See 5.3 for mechanisms.

examples.question: A polystyrene sample has molar mass 52,000 g/mol. Its repeat unit is C₈H₈, molar mass 104 g/mol. Find the average degree of polymerisation. Then find the molar mass of a polypropene (C₃H₆, 42 g/mol) sample with the same average DP.
steps: Average DP = molar mass of sample ÷ molar mass of repeat unit.
For polystyrene: average DP = 52,000 g/mol ÷ 104 g/mol = 500.
For polypropene with same average DP: molar mass = average DP × molar mass of repeat unit = 500 × 42 g/mol = 21,000 g/mol.
examples.answer: The average degree of polymerisation is 500, and the polypropene sample has molar mass 21,000 g/mol.
examples.check:
m_sample_ps = 52000
m_repeat_ps = 104
DP = m_sample_ps // m_repeat_ps
m_repeat_pp = 42
m_sample_pp = DP * m_repeat_pp
print(DP)
print(m_sample_pp)

traps: DP counts repeat units, not atoms. A DP of 500 means 500 repeat units, not 500 carbon atoms.
For condensation polymers, the repeat unit molar mass is not the monomer molar mass because a small molecule (like water) leaves. Always use the repeat unit formula.
Thermoplastic softens on heating; thermoset does not. Bakelite is a thermoset, not a thermoplastic.
Homopolymer has one monomer type; copolymer has two or more. Do not call a copolymer a homopolymer just because one monomer dominates.
Natural rubber is an elastomer, but not all elastomers are natural. Vulcanised rubber is lightly cross-linked; a thermoset is heavily cross-linked.

quiz.a: A monomer is a small molecule that can join with others. The repeat unit is the part that repeats along the polymer chain.
Degree of polymerisation (DP) is the number of repeat units in one polymer chain.

quiz.q: Explain the difference between a homopolymer and a copolymer.
quiz.a: A homopolymer has only one type of monomer. A copolymer has two or more types of monomer joined in the same chain.

quiz.q: Why must a monomer have functionality of at least two to form a polymer chain?
quiz.a: Functionality is the number of reactive sites. A monomer with only one reactive site can bond at only one end and cannot extend a chain. At least two sites allow the chain to grow.

quiz.q: A polyethene sample has molar mass 28,000 g/mol. The repeat unit is C₂H₄ (28 g/mol). Find the average degree of polymerisation.
A polymer sample softens on heating and can be remoulded. Is it likely thermoplastic or thermoset? Give one example.
quiz.a: It is likely thermoplastic because thermosets do not soften on heating. Example: polyethylene (PE).

quiz.q: A copolymer has alternating units of styrene and butadiene. What type of copolymer is it?
Why is the molar mass of a polymer sample reported as an average?
quiz.a: Because a polymer sample contains chains of different lengths (different DP values). The molar mass is an average over all chains.

beyond: Not for the exam. Industry sorts polymers by these classes to pick recycling routes: thermoplastics can be melted and remoulded, thermosets cannot. Researchers design block copolymers for drug delivery and graft copolymers as compatibilisers in blends. Search for 'polymer classification', 'degree of polymerisation', and 'copolymer architecture' to go deeper.
